IPV rule is derived (age 7 cohort and lookback window computed, not stated) and needs human review.

IPV timing not represented: minimum age 6 weeks, final dose on or after age 4 years and at least 6 months after the previous dose, and the statement that a dose is still recommended on or after age 4 even if 4+ doses were given earlier with combination vaccines. The engine only counts doses and cannot check birthdate-relative dose timing or intervals; this also covers the case of extra doses from combination vaccines.

IPV/OPV dose-validity rules not represented: only trivalent OPV counts; OPV doses before April 1, 2016 count unless given during a campaign; OPV on or after April 1, 2016 does not count; mixed OPV-IPV series. The ipv_vaccine concept may not capture valid tOPV doses.

IPV catch-up not represented: minimum ages/intervals in the first 6 months only for travel to polio-endemic regions or outbreaks (travel is uncomputable). Adolescents age 18 known or suspected to be unvaccinated or incompletely vaccinated complete a 3-dose primary series, and US-born adults may be assumed vaccinated; this depends on vaccination-history judgment. Also refers to Table 2 for other catch-up guidance.

IPV special situation not represented: adolescents aged 18 at increased risk of exposure who completed the primary series 'may administer' one lifetime booster. This is optional and depends on exposure risk (uncomputable).

Pneumococcal age 6–18 years guidance (PCV15/PCV20/PPSV23 by prior-dose history, the 8-week and 5-year intervals, and giving PCV15 before PPSV23 at separate visits) is a continuation of risk-based recommendations whose qualifying conditions are on another page. It depends on product-specific dose history and intervals, so it is not represented.
Pneumococcal vaccination in pregnancy: no recommendation due to limited data. Not a rule.

RSV nirsevimab immunization not represented. It depends on the mother's RSV vaccination status and timing (at least 14 days vs less than 14 days before delivery, or a previous pregnancy), which is not reliably in the infant's record. It also depends on birth month relative to RSV season and geography ('most of the continental United States'), with timing 'within 1 week of birth' or 'shortly before start of RSV season', which is not measurement-year relative. A rule could use the existing concept rsv_mab with uncomputable maternal-status criteria, but the age/birth-timing denominator could not be stated accurately, so it was omitted.

RSV: nirsevimab 'can be considered in rare circumstances at the discretion of healthcare providers' when the mother was vaccinated at least 14 days before delivery. This is clinician judgment and not a rule.

RSV: infants with prolonged birth hospitalization discharged October through March should be immunized shortly before or promptly after discharge. Hospitalization and discharge timing is not represented.

Footnote definitions (incomplete pneumococcal series; complete polio primary series = at least 3 doses of IPV or tOPV in any combination) and links to the mobile app and other resources are not represented as separate rules.
